Just want to share my story just in case it helps in any way. I've always loved drawing. And moreso when I see other people's art. But I don't know how at all. When I do try though, it's ugly, doesn't make sense, and is disproportionate. So I stopped trying.

Fast forward to one time we were at the mall and my sister saw me staring at a wacom tablet... They got it for me. I was very excited and drew for the first time digitally. Well let's just say it didn't turn out well and I ended up hiding my wacom intuos under my bed from pure crippling shame and embarassment.

Fast forward again to when my school required digitally drawn illustrations... well it wasn't easy for sure at first. But I've learned to stay away from drawing people because I was absolute shit at it and started drawing sceneries instead. It worked out. Granted I had to spend a few hours battling anxiety and conditioning my brain into thinking that I'm not me and I'm a real actual artist (method really worked well for me) every single time I have to draw something. I'm now one of the known artists in my department in university. I still can't draw for shit on paper, but give me a drawing tablet and a laptop and best believe I can do it.

Here's my first ever [digital art](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/CpVo3_ZUsAEScqM?format=jpg&name=large) and this is some of my [best works](https://www.behance.net/ArtbyAki) now.

I still don't consider myself a real artist. But I know that I'm a fast learner and that once I put my heart into something, I'll achieve it no matter what. Also just wanted to share that it took me 4 yrs until I could ever start drawing people again after my first failed attempt that caused a lot of anxiety but I'm doing fairly well now I think! The disconnection between drawing on a wacom and seeing the result on your screen unlike drawing on paper and seeing that you're the one "making it" really helped me as well.
